paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between the rank of fine-tuned adapters and their corresponding errors, measured in COPA. The x-axis, labeled 'Rank', has a logarithmic scale, ranging from 4 to 256, with tick labels at 4, 16, 64, and 256. The y-axis, labeled 'Errors (COPA)', has a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 0.6, with tick labels at 0.0, 0.3, and 0.6. A single line is plotted, colored black with green circular markers, and a solid line style. The line starts at approximately 0.15 on the y-axis when the rank is 4, decreases slightly to around 0.13 at a rank of 16, then increases to about 0.35 at a rank of 64, and finally rises to approximately 0.4 at a rank of 256. Error bars are also present, indicating the range of values associated with each data point.
